definitions.explanation: Music of Japanese origin, especially traditional forms played on instruments such as the koto, shamisen, and shakuhachi. Contrasts with 洋楽 (Western music).

examples.japanese: {邦楽|ほうがく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}う→習う：00479_narau⟧。
⟦{大学|だいがく}→大学：00608_daigaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{邦楽|ほうがく}⟦サークル→サークル：10933_saakuru⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{琴|こと}→琴：02152_koto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{弾|ひ}いている→弾く：02444_hiku⟧。
examples.english: I play the koto in my university's Japanese music club.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{音楽祭|おんがくさい}→音楽祭：30660_ongakusai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{邦楽|ほうがく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{洋楽|ようがく}→洋楽：18619_yougaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{両方|りょうほう}→両方：01750_ryouhou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しむ→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: At this music festival, you can enjoy both Japanese and Western music.

notes:
USAGE:
{邦楽|ほうがく} primarily refers to traditional Japanese music genres such as ⟦{雅楽|ががく}→雅楽：27354_gagaku⟧ (court music), ⟦{能楽|のうがく}→能楽：14065_nougaku⟧ (Noh music), ⟦{長唄|ながうた}→長唄：28511_nagauta⟧ (a shamisen vocal genre), and {箏曲|そうきょく} (koto music). In some contexts, it may also include modern Japanese popular music (J-pop), though the traditional meaning is more common.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {邦楽|ほうがく}: Japanese music
- ⟦{洋楽|ようがく}→洋楽：18619_yougaku⟧: Western music

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {邦楽|ほうがく}{器|き} (traditional Japanese musical instrument)
- {邦楽|ほうがく}⟦{演奏|えんそう}→演奏：01896_ensou⟧ (performance of Japanese music)
- {邦楽|ほうがく}⟦サークル→サークル：10933_saakuru⟧ (Japanese music club)

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
Do not confuse with ⟦{方角|ほうがく}→方角：08447_hougaku⟧ (direction, compass bearing), which shares the same reading.
